o1.biggest_strength: Every number traces to my October data — the $249k on 11% of revenue producing 29% of churned revenue, the blended $63.90/$120.85 prices, the +$2.7k day-one net — and its test measures the exact thing the plan depends on: switchers' churn against a control group.
o1.biggest_mistake: The largest figure in its own table (the +$41.7k retention gain at month 6) is asserted rather than derived, and its 11-channel Team comparison of $121 should be about $128 blended or $132 monthly.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the working behind the retention gain and turn the yearly-billing push into a costed second lever with its own numbers, rather than a line in the email.

o2.biggest_strength: The plan design is sharper: one user plus free client approvers protects Team while still killing the screenshots objection, and counting Team 8+ accounts with one active user before launch is exactly the right first move.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its A/B test only measures revenue from new visitors, so after eight weeks it has no evidence on the churn drop the whole recommendation rests on, and its '1 in 6' break-even contradicts its own table, which implies closer to 1 in 4.5.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Test churn on real switchers against a control, put every lifetime and break-even figure on one price basis, and stop dismissing the yearly-billing push — give it the math instead.

reason: Output 1 gives me one pick with math that ties to my numbers and a test that actually proves whether churn falls; Output 2 has the cleverer plan design and a smart pre-check on Team accounts, but its break-even '1 in 6' doesn't survive contact with its own table and its test never measures the churn drop I'm buying.
